title: In repos/goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts, inside handleRunGoal, move two tag-push statements so they run BEFORE the array
description:
In repos/goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts, inside handleRunGoal, move two tag-push statements so they run BEFORE the array they mutate is handed off.

Currently these two statements appear after the seek call:

      if (learningMode) effectiveTags.push(`learning_mode:${learningMode}`);
      if (ablation) effectiveTags.push(`ablation:${[ablation.disableReuse ? "disableReuse" : "", ablation.forceFloor ? "forceFloor" : "", ablation.pinnedPriors ? "pinnedPriors" : ""].filter(Boolean).join("+")}`);

Move both statements upward so they execute immediately after the line that begins `const effectiveTags = [...(tags ?? []), ...sigTag,` and before the object literal containing `tags: effectiveTags,`. Keep both statements byte-identical; only their position changes. Change nothing else.

Why: `effectiveTags` is passed into the seek call as `tags: effectiveTags`, and the consumer serialises the array at call time. Any push that happens after that handoff is therefore discarded. Measured on the live trace store, same array and same consumer, differing only in push position: tags composed before the handoff appear on 13,318 rows (`dispatcher_used:goal-host`) and 1,651 rows (`operator:claude-code-operator`), while tags pushed after it appear on exactly ONE row each (`execution_path:fresh_derivation`, `attempt_count:1`) out of roughly 36,000 rows.

The consequence is that a requested ablation and a held-out learning mode are both invisible in the trace: nobody can confirm from the outside that an ablation was applied, so the floor arm of a counterfactual cannot be identified afterwards, and an observe-mode run is indistinguishable from a learning one.

Only these two are movable. `execution_path`, `walk_tier` and `attempt_count` are computed from the seek result and cannot be hoisted; they need a different repair and are deliberately out of scope here. Both `learningMode` and `ablation` are parsed from the request body earlier in the same function, so they are already in scope at the earlier position.
